uslaw-usc-t2-s1881d: Section 1881d of Title 2 of the United States Code sets the date on which a set of rules takes force. It sits in Chapter 28, on the Architect of the Capitol. Its part deals with Capitol-flown flags for the kin of fallen heroes. The subchapter is to take force on 16 May 2016. One bar is set on that date. No such flag may be given under a named section till a set of rules made under a second section takes force.
uslaw-usc-t2-s661d:
Section 661d of Title 2 of the United States Code funds the credit reform system for federal loans. Under credit reform, the budget must show the true cost of direct loans and loan guarantees up front. This section authorizes the money and the accounts that make that showing possible.

Appropriations are authorized to every federal agency that may make direct loans or guarantee commitments. The sums are whatever is needed to pay the cost tied to those loans and guarantees. A second part authorizes the bookkeeping. The President may establish non-budgetary accounts where they are fitting. Those financing accounts carry the cash flows of the loan programs outside the budget totals. A third part begins in the text as the section continues. The design separates the scored cost of credit from the money that merely passes through.
